To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) Batch and Weight Normalizations are incompatible with L2 regularization; (ii) the learning rate depends on the weight scale; and (iii) ADAM does not completely eliminate this dependence.

1) L2 regularization does not have a regularizing effect when batch normalization is used; 2) L2 regularization influences the scale of weights; 3) L2 regularization also influences the effective learning rate; 4) the effective learning rate depends on the scale of the weights; 5) batch normalization influences the effective learning; 6) batch normalization influences effective learning rate in the same way that L2 regularization does, and therefore, the two can be combined.

1) L2 regularization has an effect on the scale of the weights, 2) the scale of the weight has an effect on learning rate, 3) the learning rate has an effect on convergence speed, 4) the learning rate can be controlled by the L2 regularization, 5) the L2 regularization can be replaced by a learning rate schedule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between weight decay, weight normalization and batch normalization.
the following three topics: 1) Batch normalization, 2) weight normalization, and 3) regularization.
the question of how normalization affects the effective learning rate in neural networks and how this can be controlled.

L2 regularization is not useful in combination with normalization.
L2 regularization and weight normalization are two sides of the same coin.
L2 regularization and batch normalization are not compatible, and that weight normalization and L2 regularization can be used together.
